finding: The mention graph is viable: Josephus names his imperial contemporaries abundantly and citably. But raw substring matching produced ~1 false edge per true edge. Disambiguation is the build, not an afterthought.

false_positives_caught.Ptolemy: Ptolemy Menneus, a local ruler — NOT the astronomer on the roster
false_positives_caught.Suetonius: appears only in Whiston's translator footnote, not Josephus's text
false_positives_caught.Brutus: "son of Brutus the proconsul" — Marcus’s line, NOT the legendary Lucius in the room
false_positives_caught.Josephus: self-reference — an author is not an edge to himself
false_positives_caught.Virgil: requires context check — likely a place or the poet in a note

the_three_filters_required: strip translator apparatus before scanning (the Suetonius footnote case)
full-name / epithet match, not bare first name (Ptolemy Menneus case)
consult the room-note for shared names (which Brutus)
rule: A substring match is a CANDIDATE. It becomes an edge only after the three filters AND a human confirms. Candidate-not-link, from Slip #47.
